question: The average of the first 30 natural numbers is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **average** of the first **n natural numbers** is always given by the formula: **(n + 1) ÷ 2**.

Here, the number of terms **n = 30**.

Average = (30 + 1) ÷ 2

Average = 31 ÷ 2 = 15.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First 30 natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, ..., 30.

**Formula Used:** Sum of first n natural numbers = [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2 and Average = Sum ÷ n.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e7d42e33564c4361ae44eada1faf2a232d32fcb9268276694cf3642e8a336ad.png] 

⇒ Total numbers (n) = 30

⇒ Sum = [30 × (30 + 1)] ÷ 2

⇒ Sum = 15 × 31 = 465

⇒ Average = 465 ÷ 30

⇒ Average = 15.5

**∴ The correct answer is 15.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The total sum is calculated as S = [n(n + 1)] ÷ 2.

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For any Arithmetic Progression, Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Sum of Squares and Cubes

Sum of squares = [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6 | Sum of cubes = [[n(n + 1)] ÷ 2]².

Average of First n Even/Odd Numbers

Average of first n even numbers = n + 1 | Average of first n odd numbers = n.</p
